Anya (ML): Bringing up quantized reranker v2 on staging — quick sanity check: overall ndcg@10 dropped ~3.4% vs fp16, but the regression is concentrated on short queries (<=5 tokens). Anyone seen this pattern before?
Sam: can you paste the eval command + seed + candidate ordering you used?
Anya (ML): sure, running with:
```
./eval_rerank --model rerank-v2-quant-int8 --candidates candidates.jsonl 
  --queries queries.jsonl --metric ndcg@10 --seed 12345 --stable-sort=false 
```
Anya (ML): FP16 baseline: ndcg@10=0.382. Quant (int8 gptq, per-channel): ndcg@10=0.369.
Anya (ML): Slice: queries with token_count<=5, fp16 ndcg@10=0.421 -> quant 0.387. that's a 3.4 pct absolute drop on short queries (much larger relative).
Jordan: ouch. what quant config? per-tensor/per-channel? any symmetric/asymmetric?
Anya (ML): per-channel, asymmetric, 8-bit, outlier clipping=0.995. No special kernel changes. We used the default tokenizer from the eval harness (tokenizer v1.3).
Ciara: dataset slice details? short queries often are titles or search phrases — do docs include urls/markup? tokenization differences between train and eval cause probs. did you normalize punctuation/whitespace?
Anya (ML): good point — I noticed a lot of docs in candidates.jsonl have trailing colons and small markdown blocks, e.g. "Example:
```python
...
```". we didn't strip markup.
Anya (ML): also candidate ordering might differ — we sent candidates in server-side ranking order (randomized earlier), not stable lexical sort.
Sam: try rerun with deterministic seed and stable sort, and also run with kvpack disabled (we saw kvpack + quant interact badly on short contexts).
Sam: example flags: `--seed 42 --stable-sort=true --kvpack=false`
Anya (ML): will run both. adding token normalization step too (strip code fences, collapse whitespace) — will post numbers.
eval-bot: job scheduled: eval-job-1768123490 started (rerank-v2-quant-int8 on short-query-slice). link: https://ci.redwood/evals/1768123490
Jordan: also compare MRR@10 and p@1 — ndcg can hide top-of-list regressions. If p@1 drops, that's worse for UX.
Ciara: and include a small AB on prod-like holdout (50k queries) if staging repros — maybe the model's calibration shifts on short natural-language prompts.
Anya (ML): ack. plan: (1) run deterministic eval with stable sort + normalization, (2) run kvpack off, (3) collect ndcg/mrr/p@1 per-slice, (4) if still bad, run fp16 vs int8 AB on 50k holdout. I'll post results in this thread.
Sam: thx. quick note: when you post, include the raw per-query delta sample (jsonl) so we can inspect failure modes.
Anya (ML): will include a 100-sample diff and a small script that diffs model scores.
Ciara: nice. side note — if tokenization mismatch is the culprit, a cheap fix is a pre-token-normalizer step in the eval harness; we can prod into inference pipeline later.
Anya (ML): agreed. starting the runs now :thumbsup:
